_comment: TEMPLATE — copy to .claude/settings.json and review before applying.
Kept as an example on purpose: permission grants decide what an agent may
do, so a human should be the one to apply them. Merge into an existing
settings.json rather than overwriting it.
WHY `agent-reach configure` IS DENIED OUTRIGHT: an earlier version denied
only `configure --from-browser`. That is the argument-constraining pattern
the permissions docs call fragile — reordering the flags to
`configure --platform xueqiu --from-browser chrome` walks straight past it.
Credentials are attached by a human in a terminal, never by an agent, so
the whole subcommand is denied and nothing has to match a flag.
WHAT THIS CANNOT DO: permission rules gate tool EXECUTION. They cannot stop
an agent printing a command for you to paste yourself. That boundary lives
in CLAUDE.md, and it is guidance, not enforcement — treat a command an
agent hands you as a suggestion to judge, not an instruction to run.
TRUST NOTE on the SessionStart hook: enabling it means every commit to
scripts/agent-reach-preflight.sh is code that runs automatically the next
time a session starts in this directory — including on a contributor's
branch you checked out to review. Do NOT swap it for the installer.
The allow bucket's safety also depends on the pinned upstream commit —
see .claude/skills/agent-reach/UPSTREAM.md.
